newsitem.title: GERMANY: Van Miert criticises Deutsche Telekom.
newsitem.headline: Van Miert criticises Deutsche Telekom.

text.p: European competition commissioner Karel van Miert was quoted in a German newspaper on Wednesday as criticising the prices Deutsche Telekom plans to charge rivals for using its telecommunications network.
Competitors have complained that Telekom is demanding too much for access to its network after the German telecommunications market is opened up from January next year.

The privatised giant has insisted that its charges must be high to take account of the huge costs it has incurred by building a state-of-the art network in Germany's "new states" -- the former communist east of the country.

"The charges Telekom is demanding from competitors are far too high, even when you take account of Telekom's special situation because of investments in the new states," the Die Welt daily quoted Van Miert as saying in an early edition of Thursday's paper.
It said the commissioner was concerned that the prices demanded by Telekom could "kill competition from the start." Van Miert said the company's policy was creating "substantial problems."
Van Miert also said the commission was still studying expert opinions about whether Telekom should be forced to divest its cable television network.
Some rivals and politicians have demanded the company take this step to encourage competition.
Van Miert did not say what decision he might reach. But the paper quoted him as saying: "I can hardly imagine that things will stay as they are just now."
